defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: isinstance(TextIO) always False, string-path file never closed in stop()
default log_output=None devnull BufferedWriter never closed
DEVNULL guard removed; os.close(-3) called on subprocess.DEVNULL
double stop() raises OSError on int fd since try/except removed
no test for string-path log_output closing (pre-existing)
no test for default log_output=None closing (pre-existing)
votes.evidence_quote: `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` always returns `False`. `typing.TextIO` is a type-checking special form with no runtime `__instancecheck__` support — it does not behave like `io.TextIOBase`.
votes.justification: The review identifies the root cause in stop(): the isinstance(TextIO) check never matches a real file, so file logs are left open. It also covers the BufferedWriter devnull case and proposes the io-based fix. The second finding repeats the same defect for the default devnull log, which is part of the known defect.
